items.title: fleet actions exec: live short-lived exec sessions inside Actions runners, coordinator-handed-off
items.body:
# fleet actions exec: live short-lived exec sessions inside Actions runners, coordinator-handed-off

Drew's order, 2026-11-23 15:17 CST: implement an alternate `fleet actions exec` mode that may become the primary — agents connect into GitHub Actions runners and exec commands themselves, temporary and short-lived like the commander/route subcommand family (#13717). The central coordinator (#13765) establishes the connection handoff; the fleet command background-watches the run after handoff.

## Premise (verified first-hand, 2026-11-23)

- **Coordinator (#13765)** has a complete design of record: broker verbs `/placement-claim|confirm|release|claim-status|load`, a coordinator sweep in the queue broker, client integration with a **singular fallback** that names itself via `placement_path`. Its build is routed separately; this mode composes with the design (claim a slot for the session's host surface when the verbs answer; proceed singular and record `placement_path` when they don't) and never forks it.
- **Fleet action constellation:** the generic fleet action lives in **dezren39/fleet** — composite action `.github/actions/fleet-command`, dispatch workflows `fleet-command.yml` (repo-queue dispatch runner) and `fleet-run.yml` (generic runner; developing-today/fleet fork adds runner choice + cache deltas that must survive syncs). Fixes land on dezren39/fleet main and sync to the forks.
- **Existing IO pattern (dispatch path):** command output lives in the Actions run log; reusable output chains via the `fleet-output` artifact (`previous_run_id` input downloads the prior run's artifact); caches via actions/cache and the R2 nix cache (`cache.push_nix` → signed `nix copy` to the R2 cache URL, skipping quietly when secrets are absent).
- **PM push surface exists:** `crates/fleet-queue/src/needs_drew.rs` (#8568) emits needs-drew alerts into the PM aggregator throat — `POST http://127.0.0.1:4870/api/alerts`, Bearer token resolved **by name** through fleet-secrets, body `{source, key, severity, title, body, needsDrew:{ledgerId, question, context, options[], links[]}}`, deduped by (source, key). The notification presents choices; this is the emergency-extension push path.
- **Rendezvous constraint (#10356):** the sandbox has no inbound path; every route names its rendezvous. Runners are on the public internet and the queue broker lives on the laptop — so this mode needs a public door in the commander/mcpx pattern (Worker gate + tunnel → laptop), path-scoped to the session verbs.
- **Route family shape (#13717):** timeout required by construction; the serving form is named in output.

## Method survey — direct runner access, filtered by the public-log leak

The hard filter: **most off-the-shelf runner-access methods print SSH/connection info into the run log, and in a public repo the log is world-readable.** Any method whose connection material can appear in logs is disqualified, however convenient.

| Method | Shape | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tmate (mxschmitt/action-tmate et al.) | Runner opens tmate session; SSH string + web URL printed to log | **Rejected** — connection string in public logs is the exact leak |
| upterm (action-upterm) | SSH via upterm server; connection info printed to log; actor-limiting exists | **Rejected** — same leak; allowlists don't unpublish the log |
| tailscale/github-action | Runner joins the tailnet; reach it by tailnet name, nothing secret prints | Viable but not picked: couples runner access to tailnet enrolment/ACLs for every caller, and #13752 thread 1 is actively designing *away* from Tailscale-only reach |
| cloudflared + Access on the runner | Runner dials out to Cloudflare; requester authenticates via Access | Viable; the estate already runs this door pattern (commander/mcpx). Kept as the door technology, not the session protocol |
| iroh endpoint on the runner | NodeId is a public key — printing it leaks nothing; auth is the keypair (#13752 thread 2) | Right long-term transport for the fleet binary; not the v1 session protocol (pilot is scoped to seat→amd, and this mode needs the coordinator handoff semantics first). The session protocol below is transport-shaped so iroh can carry it later |
| **Runner-side agent dials OUT to the coordinator (chosen)** | The workflow starts a small agent (a mode of the fleet binary). The agent proves it is inside the run with the job's **GitHub OIDC token** (fetched from the Actions runtime, never logged), registers with the broker, and holds an outbound long-poll. Commands flow requester → broker → agent; IO flows back the same way | **Chosen** — no inbound path, nothing connection-shaped ever exists outside the two endpoints, the session handle is a public identifier (safe in logs), and the handoff *is* the coordinator's job in #13765's design |

Runner-side auth detail: the broker verifies the OIDC JWT against GitHub's JWKS and checks `repository`, `workflow`, `job_workflow_ref`, `run_id`, `run_attempt` claims against the session row the coordinator created at dispatch. Requester-side auth is the existing broker seat auth. Workflow inputs carry only the handle + non-secret parameters — never a token (inputs are visible on the run page; secrets would be masked but dispatch cannot receive them).

## Design

**Three pieces, one flow.**
1. **Action** — dezren39/fleet `.github/actions/fleet-exec-session` (composite, fleet-command conventions): sets up the pinned fleet binary, runs `fleet actions agent` for the session, ships the egress helper on PATH.
2. **Workflow** — dezren39/fleet `.github/workflows/fleet-exec.yml` (workflow_dispatch; inputs: handle, target repo/ref optional checkout, runner, lease/max seconds, hide-logs flag; `permissions: id-token: write`; job timeout = max lifespan + grace).
3. **Subcommand** — new `actions` domain in pkgs/fleet (fleet-registry + verbs.md in the same change): `fleet actions exec` group in the #13717 family shape — `--timeout` required by construction, serving form named in output.

**Flow:** requester runs `fleet actions exec start` → subcommand asks the coordinator to claim a slot for the host surface and create the session row (singular fallback per #13765 when the coordinator doesn't answer) → subcommand dispatches `fleet-exec.yml` with the handle → coordinator/subcommand binds run id + attempt (the **handoff**: handle, `OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID`, attempt) → runner agent registers via OIDC → requester execs via `fleet actions exec run <handle> -- cmd`, attaches/streams, renews, closes.

**Broker verbs** (new module `crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue/actions_exec.rs`, routed in `turso_queue::dispatch` beside the placement coordinator's; house conditional-UPDATE atomicity; DDL beside `placement_sessions`):
- `/actions-exec-open` (seat) — create session {handle, host_repo, seat, lease_until, max_until, hide_logs, state}.
- `/actions-exec-bind` (seat/coordinator) — record run_id + attempt.
- `/actions-exec-register` (agent, OIDC-verified) — bind agent to session, state `live`.
- `/actions-exec-poll` (agent) — long-poll for commands + lease state.
- `/actions-exec-command` (seat) — enqueue one command {cmd_id, text, timeout_s}.
- `/actions-exec-io` (agent) — append IO chunk {cmd_id, seq, stream, data}; `/actions-exec-result` (agent) — exit code, cmd terminal.
- `/actions-exec-stream` (seat) — IO chunks after a seq (attach + background watch read this).
- `/actions-exec-renew` (seat) — extend lease within max; past max → `extension-required`.
- `/actions-exec-extend-request` (seat) — past-max extension: creates the request **and emits the needs-drew alert** (source `fleet-actions-exec`, key `actions-exec-ext:<handle>`, options approve/deny, links to the run + this issue). Session enters `extension-pending` with a short decision grace so a live agent isn't killed mid-question.
- `/actions-exec-extend-decide` (seat acting on Drew's answer) — applies or denies. **Known gap:** the phone tap → broker write-back is the PM stack's next phase; v1's write-back is a seat running this verb on Drew's recorded answer. The alert is the push; the verb is the closest existing surface.
- `/actions-exec-close` (either side) — terminal; agent exits, workflow step ends.

**Disconnect tolerance:** requester disconnect is a non-event (broker holds commands, IO, lease). Agent network blips retry with backoff against the long-poll. Reconnect = re-attach with the same handle; the session and any running command survive a short grace window, mirroring the laptop attach pattern.

**Lease discipline:** lease = `--timeout` at start (required, no default). Hard cap = `--max-lifespan` (default 30 min, ceiling 120 min — the fleet-run leg cap). The agent enforces the lease locally as well as via the broker (dies at expiry even if partitioned, after a final IO/egress flush). Renewals move `lease_until` up to `max_until`; past that, only an approved emergency extension (push above) moves it, each approval bounded (+30 min).

**File egress:** the Action puts `fleet-exec-put <file>` on the session PATH: it copies the file into the session outbox (uploaded as the `fleet-exec-out` workflow artifact when the session step ends) **and** PUTs it to R2 (S3-compatible; credentials arrive as workflow secrets, are masked by GitHub, and are never echoed; absent credentials skip the R2 leg quietly, the fleet-run cache pattern).

**Log visibility + IO decision:** by default the agent echoes session IO to its own stdout, so commands and output land in the Actions run log (the dispatch path's existing visibility). `--hide-logs` on the subcommand turns the echo off. **Decision:** the transport is brokered in both modes (it is the handoff mechanism, not a visibility feature); the broker's IO chunk store is the cache of record either way — with logs visible it is the low-latency attach/watch source, with logs hidden it is the *only* IO path back to the requester. No second IO system is built.

**Background watch:** after handoff the subcommand can follow the run without holding the requester's terminal: `fleet actions exec watch <handle>` streams broker IO + run status (polled via the placement GitHub client) until terminal; `start --detach` returns after handoff and records the handle in the local session store so `watch`/`attach`/`run` resolve it from any seat (the portable `OWNER/REPO#RUN_ID` form works too).

## Slices

1. This issue: premise + survey + design.
2. Action + workflow in dezren39/fleet (agent bootstrap in proof mode: build the agent from a code ref in the runner; production pins the released fleet binary).
3. Broker verbs + DDL + tests (rusqlite fake-pipeline pattern from #13765's proof bar).
4. Runner agent (`fleet actions agent`): OIDC register, poll/exec/stream loop, lease enforcement, egress helper.
5. Subcommand (`fleet actions exec` group): start/run/attach/watch/renew/extend/close + coordinator composition + singular fallback naming.
6. PM push wiring for emergency extension (needs-drew throat emission + decide verb).
7. Live proof (below), runbook note in `doc/agents/remote-build-and-test.md`, verbs.md, PRs, merge on green.

## Proof bar

One live end-to-end run, recorded here: subcommand → coordinator handoff (handle + run id + attempt named) → exec a command on the runner → `fleet-exec-put` a file out to **both** the workflow artifact and R2 → requester disconnect/reconnect resumes the same session → renewal extends within the cap → a short-lease session dies at its cap unrenewed. Plus the leak acceptance test: **read the produced public workflow logs end to end and show no connection material** (no tokens, no OIDC material, no credential values — handles and run ids only).

Lane ACTIONS-EXEC. If the platform execution-risk check stops a build step, the stop is recorded here with the exact slice state for routing to a laptop session.

items.title: design: transport adapter contract — declarations, levels, asymmetric routing (multi-transport head)
items.body:
# Design: the transport adapter contract (multi-transport head design)

Parent epic: #13926 — Multi-transport reach: any protocol as a carrier. Direction recorded on #13752 (comment 7118605020). This is the programme's head design: everything else in the epic plugs into the contract defined here.

## 1. Problem + context (with evidence)

Drew's direction (2026-11-23): the P2P / ID / fleet stack should be reachable over many alternate transports and proxied alternate systems — Spritely-style relays, Tor, Noise, ActivityPub, ATProto, email, MQTT, HTTP/REST, MCP, IRC, Zulip, Slack, Discord bots, Gopher, Gemini, telnet beside SSH, physical media — each at a declared level (read / bidirectional / write-capable / sync-equivalent), with **asymmetric send/receive paths as a first-class requirement** ("send over carrier pigeon, receive over fax" is a design requirement, not a joke).

Today every path we have invented its own shape, because no contract exists:

- The **bridge** (#13895) is an HTTP note transport with class/name addressing and token-gated send — its own addressing, its own gating.
- The **mcpx door** (#13657, live) is an MCP endpoint with its own gate/proxy rules.
- **Email** exists in the #13752 design as a bootstrap carrier for signed tickets — introductions only, no message contract.
- **Sneakernet bundles** (#13889) carry signed data + grants for ID — a sync-shaped path designed inside the ID-graph programme only.

Four instances, four shapes. Each new carrier added ad hoc multiplies integration and security-review cost, and nothing today can express "reachable at read level over X, writable over Y, replies come back over Z" — the asymmetry Drew requires.

## 2. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**

- One adapter contract that every carrier family in the epic's inventory can be expressed in without special cases.
- Every adapter **declares** its properties up front (machine-readable), including its level per direction.
- Asymmetric routing as a core property of the message envelope, not an adapter feature.
- Identity on every path binds back to the fleet CA / ID identity — or the gap is explicitly declared (proxies).
- Levels are **proven live** before they are recorded as held.

**Non-goals**

- Building all adapters now (this design sequences them; most are later children of the epic).
- Replacing or altering the primary broker/iroh path (#13752 pilot stays broker-ticket-first).
- Anonymity guarantees of our own (a Tor adapter carries Tor's properties; the contract claims none).
- Solving platform terms-of-service questions for bot proxies — the contract records the trust/custody facts; acceptability is decided per adapter.

## 3. Alternatives considered

- **Do nothing; keep adding transports ad hoc.** Cheapest this quarter; the four existing instances show the cost curve — every new path re-invents addressing, gating, and metering, and asymmetry stays inexpressible. Rejected.
- **One central gateway service translating everything.** Single custody and trust point; contradicts the federated/stateless direction of the relay work and #13752. Rejected.
- **Adopt a multi-transport library wholesale (libp2p-style).** Strong for overlay transports; silent on email, chat proxies, federation protocols, and physical media. Kept as a component choice *inside* individual adapters, not as the contract.
- **A thin contract: declaration + routing core, adapters independent (chosen).** The contract standardises only what must agree — declarations, envelope, routing, gating, metering — and leaves each adapter's internals free.

## 4. The contract

### 4.1 What every adapter must declare

A machine-readable **adapter declaration** (the registry entry):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name`, `version` | Adapter identity |
| `shape` | `transport` or `proxy` (see §4.4) |
| `addressing` | How a peer/user is named on this carrier, and the mapping to fleet-CA / ID identity |
| `levels` | Level held **per direction** (send / receive), from §4.2 |
| `delivery` | At-most-once / at-least-once; ordering guarantee; whether causal metadata survives; latency class; size limits; offline behaviour |
| `identity_binding` | `cryptographic` (end-to-end, both ends are our stack) / `mapped` (proxy-held mapping table) / `none` (public read-only) |
| `capability_gating` | What capability a sender needs at each level; how revocation reaches this path |
| `metering` | What is counted (messages / bytes / actions) and where the counter lives |
| `custody` (proxies only) | Who holds the platform credentials; the platform trust statement; the translation boundary (§4.4) |

### 4.2 The four levels, defined precisely

- **read** — the adapter delivers inbound messages/observations to the stack. No outbound path exists or is used. (Delivery semantics still matter: read over email is durable and complete; read over a chat system is an editable, deletable stream. The declaration says which.)
- **bidirectional** — messages flow both ways over this adapter. Not necessarily one connection: an email adapter declaring SMTP-out + IMAP-in is one adapter at bidirectional.
- **write-capable** — the stack can originate *state-changing actions* on the far side (post, publish, execute), not merely messages. Distinct from bidirectional because writes carry authority: this level requires the capability-gating declaration to be non-empty.
- **sync-equivalent** — the adapter can carry the data plane's full sync protocol (per #13779's compositions) with convergence intact: causal metadata survives, bulk transfer works, withholding/replay behaviour is declared. Reference instances: sneakernet bundles (#13889), iroh-class transports.

### 4.3 Asymmetric routing rules

1. Every message envelope carries an explicit **reply route** (adapter + address). A sender never assumes the reply arrives on the path it sent on.
2. The routing core selects the send adapter and the expected receive adapter **independently**; a route is a (send, receive) pair, either side of which may be any registered adapter at a sufficient level.
3. Delivery receipts, where an adapter supports them, travel the declared reply route.
4. Timeouts and failure handling are per-direction: a dead send path says nothing about the receive path.
5. Level checks apply per direction against the *pair*: e.g. a write sent over a write-capable adapter may legitimately receive its result over a read-level adapter.

### 4.4 Transport adapter vs proxied alternate system

Drew listed both shapes deliberately; the contract treats them differently.

- A **transport adapter** carries the stack's own messages end-to-end. The far end is another instance of our stack (or a peer implementing the same contract). Identity binds cryptographically at both ends; the carrier sees framing/ciphertext, not content or authority.
- A **proxied alternate system** terminates at a platform we do not control — a Discord/Zulip/Slack bot, an ActivityPub server. The proxy speaks the platform's protocols in the platform's identity model; messages are *translated* at the proxy boundary; the far end may be a human, not our stack. Identity binding is a **mapping table held by the proxy**, not a cryptographic property of the path. The platform can read, retain, rate-limit, and revoke.

Consequences in the contract: a proxy must additionally declare `custody` (who holds the platform credentials), the **translation boundary** (which message types survive translation, and what is lost), and a **trust statement** (what the platform operator can see and do). Gating differs: a transport adapter gates by capability end-to-end; a proxy gates *at the proxy*, whose own authority is its platform identity plus its mapping table — so a compromised proxy can forge within its platform scope, and proxy declarations must state that scope as a ceiling.

### 4.5 Security analysis per level

- **read:** inbound injection and spoofing are the risks. Per the #13752 ticket doctrine, the carrier is untrusted: authenticate the payload (signatures, CA binding), never the channel. A read adapter must not let carrier-side metadata (sender fields, headers) become identity claims.
- **bidirectional:** adds session confusion and cross-path correlation, plus **downgrade**: a peer reachable at sync level on a strong path must not be trickable into accepting write authority asserted over a weaker path. Authority claims are verified against the capability, not the path — and the path's declared level caps what may be *accepted* from it.
- **write-capable:** adds authority amplification and confused-deputy risk (worst at proxies, §4.4). Revocation propagation must be declared: on a store-and-forward path (email, sneakernet), a revoked capability may still be in flight — the receiving side verifies at receipt time, never at send time.
- **sync-equivalent:** adds full-state exposure to the path and convergence attacks (withholding, replay, selective delivery on store-and-forward media). Bundles verify before merge (#13889's rule); replay windows and ordering claims live in the `delivery` declaration.

### 4.6 Data model

Three durable objects: the **adapter declaration** (above), the **route** (a named (send-adapter, receive-adapter, address-mapping) triple a peer or service is reachable by), and the **envelope** (payload + reply route + capability reference + per-path metadata the declared delivery semantics require). No other shared state; adapters keep their own internals.

## 5. Proposed first-adapter order (grounded in what exists)

1. **HTTP/REST, by formalising the bridge** (#13895) — code exists; proves the declaration shape against a real adapter at near-zero build cost.
2. **Email** — already designed as a bootstrap carrier in #13752 (Delta Chat pattern is researched); store-and-forward makes it the natural first proof of asymmetric routing.
3. **MCP, by formalising the mcpx door** (#13657) — live today; validates the contract against a request/response tool protocol rather than a message protocol.
4. **MQTT** — first true pub/sub bus; small, well-understood; its QoS levels stress-test the delivery-semantics vocabulary.
5. **Sneakernet bundles** — rides #13889's D4 design; becomes the sync-equivalent reference instance.
6. **IRC as the first proxied system** — simplest chat shape, relay-friendly, no platform gatekeeper; then Zulip / Slack / Discord bots under the proven proxy rules.
7. **Federation protocols (ActivityPub, ATProto)** — largest surface; their native identity models must be reconciled with the CA binding deliberately.
8. **Overlay/relay transports (Spritely-style Noise XK relays, Tor)** — deepest work; builds on #13752's own roadmap.
9. **Gopher / Gemini / telnet** — small, well-specified; cheap wins that prove less about the contract, so they are opportunistic (any free lane) rather than sequenced blockers.

## 6. Build slices (dependency-ordered; each sized for one lane/session)

- **S1 — Contract + declaration schema + registry.** The §4 contract as a dated design record in doc/ plus a machine-readable declaration schema and a registry home. *Acceptance:* the four existing instances (bridge, mcpx door, email-bootstrap, sneakernet) are each expressed as declarations with no special cases; schema validation runs in CI.
- **S2 — Routing core.** Envelope with explicit reply route; independent send/receive adapter selection; per-direction level checks. *Acceptance:* loopback test adapters demonstrate the pigeon/fax case in tests — send via adapter A, reply via adapter B — plus downgrade rejection (§4.5).
- **S3 — Bridge formalised as the HTTP adapter.** *Acceptance:* bridge registered with its true levels; existing behaviour unchanged; metering counters emitted.
- **S4 — Email adapter.** *Acceptance:* live round trip between two stack identities over email only; cross-adapter asymmetric proof (email out, HTTP in) passes; revocation verified at receipt.
- **S5 — MCP adapter formalisation.** *Acceptance:* mcpx door expressed as a declaration; a tool call routed through the contract's envelope.
- **S6 — MQTT adapter.** *Acceptance:* pub/sub round trip; declared QoS mapping honoured; offline queueing matches the declaration.
- **S7 — Proxy shape proven with IRC.** *Acceptance:* custody/translation/trust declarations written and reviewed; read + bidirectional live; write off by default and gated when enabled.
- **S8 — Sneakernet adapter formalisation** (with #13889). *Acceptance:* bundle round trip declared and proven sync-equivalent; verify-before-merge enforced.

Follow-on families (federation, overlays/Tor, Gopher/Gemini, telnet, Zulip/Slack/Discord) are filed as children of #13926 once S1–S8 evidence exists, in the §5 order.

## 7. Rollout + rollback

The contract is additive: nothing existing changes behaviour. Adapters join by registering a declaration; an adapter is disabled by removing its registration (one flip, mirroring the provider enable/disable rule). Rollback for any slice is deregistration; the primary broker/iroh path is untouched throughout.

## 8. Verification plan

- A **conformance test kit** from S2 onward: every new adapter runs the same suite — declaration validation, per-level live proof, the asymmetry test, metering check — before its levels are recorded as held.
- Each slice's acceptance criteria (above) are verified live, with the proof recorded on the slice's issue.
- Security checks from §4.5 are test cases, not review comments: downgrade rejection (S2), receipt-time revocation (S4), proxy scope ceiling (S7).

## 9. Open questions (each with a named decider)

- **Q1.** Does the contract live at the fleet layer, the ID layer, or a shared library both consume? — **Decider: Drew** (on Archer's recommendation; the four instances span both layers today).
- **Q2.** May a proxied system ever hold sync-equivalent? (Recommendation: no — proxies cap at write-capable.) — **Decider: Drew.**
- **Q3.** Metering: per-adapter counters only, or unified into the fleet/PM metering plane? — **Decider: Archer** (implementation detail within the existing metering direction).
- **Q4.** Telnet: in scope only behind a relay/overlay, never plaintext on an uncontrolled segment? — **Decider: Drew.**
- **Q5.** Federation identity (ActivityPub/ATProto): fleet-CA cross-certification, or mapping-table treatment like proxies? — **Decider: Drew.**

## Links

Epic #13926 · transport design #13752 · P2P synthesis #13779 · ID-graph epic #13880 · sneakernet D4 #13889 · bridge #13895 · mcpx door #13657 · ID wire-format neighbour #5674

items.title: cold-store-reaper: s3_list_objects loops forever on a truncated page with a missing, empty, or repeated continuation token

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/cold-store-reaper
labels.description: Package/app: cold-store-reaper (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

items.body:
## Summary

`ColdStore.s3_list_objects` (`pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py:1555-1569`) paginates ListObjectsV2 with no progress guard: it loops `while True`, extending the result list, and returns only when a page says `IsTruncated` is false. If a page claims truncation but carries no usable continuation token — or repeats the token just used — the loop re-requests the same page forever, appending duplicate objects and growing memory without bound. There is no error, no page cap, and no token-progress check.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `ed8e5910`)

- `s3_list_objects` (cold_store.py:1559-1569): `token = None`; each iteration builds `query = {"list-type": "2"}` and adds `continuation-token` only `if token:` (:1561-1563 — an empty-string token is dropped too), calls `_s3_request`, extends `out`, and returns only `if not truncated`.
- `_parse_s3_list_page` (cold_store.py:138-172) returns `token = None` when the `NextContinuationToken` element is absent (:149, :154-155) and `child.text` verbatim otherwise — it never cross-checks the token against truncation.
- Probe on the laptop driving the real module (cold_store.py sha256 `d3fe48c5` identical in both clones; `_s3_request` stubbed to serve canned ListObjectsV2 pages; probe + log in the fleet's `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-28-laneB-s3list/`):
  - CONTROL — page 1 truncated with token `tok2`, page 2 not truncated: terminates, 2 calls, 3 objects.
  - BUG-A — every page `IsTruncated=true`, no `NextContinuationToken` element: still looping past the probe's 12-call cap (the first page is re-requested with no token each time).
  - BUG-B — every page truncated and repeats the same token `tokX`: still looping past the cap (each iteration re-requests the identical page and appends its objects again).
  - BUG-C — truncated with an empty token element: still looping past the cap (`if token:` drops it, same as BUG-A).
  - Probe run twice, identical results.
- Existing tests cover only well-behaved pagination: the FakeS3 server in tests/test_cold_store.py always emits a fresh `NextContinuationToken` when truncated (:760-785), and `test_list_pagination` (:1318-1332) asserts the 2/2/1 happy path. No test serves a truncated page with a missing, empty, or repeated token.
- Callers inherit the hang: `backup_supabase` (cold_store.py:1775) and the eviction scan (:1832) both start from `s3_list_objects`, so one malformed listing page wedges the nightly backup / evict-scan with no diagnostic — the same class of silent first-request death this package has been hardening against (cf. the transport-retry and curl-fallback work in #1625).

Real S3/R2 normally sends a token with `IsTruncated=true`, but this client already treats the endpoint as untrusted at every other layer (byte-count verification, transport retries, torn-body handling); a non-conforming, proxied, or partially corrupted listing response should be a loud `ColdStoreError`, not an infinite loop with unbounded memory growth in a long-lived nightly job.

## Why it matters

`backup-supabase` and `evict-scan` are unattended nightly paths. A single bad listing page turns them into a silent infinite loop: the job never completes, never errors, and accumulates duplicate object entries in memory until it is killed — indistinguishable from a slow run until someone notices the backup is stale.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `s3_list_objects` raises `ColdStoreError` (naming the bucket) when a truncated page arrives with a missing or empty `NextContinuationToken`.
- [ ] `s3_list_objects` raises `ColdStoreError` when the returned continuation token does not advance (equals the token used for the current request), instead of re-requesting the same page.
- [ ] Well-behaved multi-page listings behave exactly as today (existing `test_list_pagination` and the S3 transport-retry tests pass unchanged).
- [ ] New tests cover the missing-token, empty-token, and repeated-token pages and assert the call count stays bounded (the listing aborts on the offending page, it does not keep fetching).

items.title: cold-store-reaper v2: D1 manifest sync, DB-backup class, rehydrator Worker
items.body: Extends `pkgs/cold-store-reaper` (v1: PR #923) with the next three build steps from the cold-store design. ## 1. `sync-manifest` Pushes the local SQLite manifest (objects, bundles, members, transfer_ledger, meta) to the Cloudflare D1 database `cold-store-manifest` via the D1 REST query API, as batched idempotent upserts (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT() DO UPDATE`, primary keys read from `schema.sql` via PRAGMA). Token from `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` env only; account/db ids from env overrides, `state.json`, or the built-in defaults. `--dry-run` prints per-table row/statement counts and contacts nothing. Non-200 / `success:false` fails with a clear error; partial runs resume by re-running (upserts). ## 2. DB-backup class (design section 5) - `ensure-folders` also creates `supabase/`, `turso/`, `d1/` under the app-owned `db-backups/` (idempotent, IDs in `state.json`). - `put-backup `: unbundled upload as `--`, `backup-upload` ledger row, prints the Drive file id. - `list-backups [--db ]`: newest first. - Retention enforcement (30/12/12, trash-not-delete) is explicitly **out of scope** and noted as pending in the README. ## 3. Rehydrator Worker (`worker/`) - `GET /health` (no auth); `GET /fetch/` with `Authorization: Bearer ` (401 without). - D1 binding `MANIFEST` lookup objects→members→bundles; `BundleFlight` Durable Object keyed by bundle id single-flights concurrent pulls, caches the Google access token in DO storage, Range-pulls exactly one zstd frame from Drive, decompresses, sha256-verifies — 404 unknown sha, 502 on any Drive/decode/hash failure, never serves unverified bytes. - zstd decoding vendored via **fzstd** (pure JS), bundled by esbuild into the single self-contained `worker/dist/worker.js` (force-added past `**/dist`; `node --check` clean). `wrangler.toml.example` documents bindings for the operator's API-driven deploy. - Local proof (`npm test`): packs a real bundle with the Python reaper, decodes a member frame (non-zero offset) with `src/decoder.js` — the identical module bundled into dist — and asserts the sha256. ## Tests `python3 -m unittest discover -s pkgs/cold-store-reaper/tests` — **16 tests, all passing**: - v1 suite (7) unchanged except the ensure-folders count 4→7 for the new backup subfolders. - New: fake-D1 sync (dry-run counts contact nothing; upsert SQL shape/auth/path; HTTP-500 and missing-token errors), backups (subfolders created once, dated naming, folder routing, ledger row, newest-first listing), and the worker decoder proof (skips cleanly when node/node_modules are absent). - Fake Drive extended with file listings + monotonic createdTime. No real Google/Cloudflare calls anywhere. Formatters run as in v1 (ruff format, biome, prettier); treefmt now excludes the esbuild dist output (generated artifact, same treatment as package-lock.json). --- Need help on this PR? items.title: cold-store-reaper v1: Google Drive cold-store CLI (pack / resumable upload+verify / range fetch)
items.body: ## What New `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/`: a stdlib-only Python 3.12 CLI that archives files into Google Drive as a cold, immutable store and restores individual objects back out. Commands: `init`, `auth-url`, `auth-exchange`, `ensure-folders`, `pack`, `upload`, `fetch`, `status`. ## Design points - **Bundle format:** each input file becomes its own zstd frame (via the `zstd` CLI); frames are concatenated into `b_.csb`. Bundles are immutable — a changed set is a new bundle. - **Manifest:** local SQLite using the canonical cold-store schema verbatim (`schema.sql` in the package): objects / bundles / members (byte offset+length per frame) / transfer_ledger / meta (3 TiB budget, 700 GB/day upload hard stop). - **Upload** is resumable + chunked; after completion it compares Drive's `md5Checksum`+size against local values and only then marks the bundle `verified`, flips its objects to `cold`, and writes a ledger row. - **Fetch** Range-downloads exactly one object's frame, decompresses it, and verifies the object sha256 before writing output. - **Identity:** the OAuth app holds ONLY the `drive.file` scope, so it can see nothing but files it creates. On first run it creates its own root folder `Cold Store Reaper` (subfolders `bundles/`, `manifests/`, `db-backups/`) and remembers IDs in `state.json`. Trees created by other apps are invisible to it and are never referenced by ID. - **Credentials:** `client_id`/`client_secret`/`refresh_token` live in a mode-600 `credentials.json` under `$COLD_STORE_HOME` (default `~/.config/cold-store/`), materialized by the operator from Bitwarden; secret values are never printed or committed. No real Google API calls are made by this PR or its tests (no grant exists yet). ## Tests ``` $ python3 -m unittest discover -s pkgs/cold-store-reaper/tests -v Ran 7 tests in ~20s — OK ``` All tests run offline against a fake Drive HTTP server (token endpoint, folder create/list, resumable upload sessions incl. 308 resume, files.get md5/size, Range downloads): - `TestAuth`: consent URL shape (scope/access_type/prompt/redirect); exchange stores the refresh token at mode 600 without echoing it. - `TestPack`: manifest rows, member offsets, frame extraction by offset/length, decompress+sha256 round-trip. - `TestUploadFetch`: ensure-folders idempotence; multi-chunk upload -> verified (Drive md5 matches) -> objects cold -> fetch round-trip byte-identical; ledger rows for both directions; unknown-object fetch errors. - `TestStatus`: counts/cold-bytes arithmetic, rolling-24h ledger window (a 3-day-old row is excluded), hard-stop + budget flags. Also smoke-tested the real CLI offline: `init` -> `pack` -> `status` against a temp `$COLD_STORE_HOME`. ## Not in v1 R2-eviction reaper loop, DB-backup path, rehydrator Worker path, compaction — later steps of the design's build order. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(browsers): structural WebDriver BiDi for Firefox + Zen on loopback (code#5924)
items.body: Companion to #6123 (CDP for the Chromium family). The Firefox family has no CDP — its remote protocol is WebDriver BiDi, started by `--remote-debugging-port`. Drew's order 2026-11-05: enable BiDi on all, same structural way. **Ports** (one fleet table, loopback-only): 19222 Helium CDP · 19223 Brave/Chrome CDP · 19224 Chromium CDP · **19225 Firefox BiDi · 19226 Zen BiDi** · 19227 Zen Twilight BiDi (darwin). **Mechanism:** bin-only `symlinkJoin` wrappers in the `chromiumCdp` shape (both packages' desktop files use bare `Exec=` names resolved through PATH, so bin wrapping covers launcher launches). `firefoxBidi` + `zenBidi` in `nixos/environment` systemPackages; the same wrapper is `programs.firefox.package` in home/common; raw `firefox` removed from the three user package lists (the wrapped system package serves all users). **Flags:** `--remote-debugging-port` only. The remote agent binds 127.0.0.1 itself; there is no address flag in the Firefox agent. Default Host/Origin policy kept deliberately — verified on Firefox 159: foreign Host → 400, Origin-bearing upgrade → 400, so web content can't hijack the socket; local tooling (no Origin) works as-is. No `--remote-allow-origins`. **Verification:** both derivations built and wrapper scripts inspected; amd, nixos, and vm_amd configs evaluate; HM package evaluates to `firefox-159.0-bidi`; **live proof** with isolated throwaway profiles through the *built wrapper binaries*: `WebDriver BiDi listening on ws://127.0.0.1:19225` (Firefox 159.0) and `:19226` (Zen 1.23.1b), each answering a WebSocket `session.status` round trip at `/session` (101 + `{"result":{"ready":true}}`). Note the endpoint path is `/session` in current Firefox — `/` is only the httpd status page. No switch run; activation rides the next system switch, alongside the staged CDP/Sunshine work. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: cold-store-reaper: live Google access token is cached in state.json, which the README calls '(no secrets)' and which is written without 0600 permissions

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Not yet triaged; needs a first look

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/cold-store-reaper
labels.description: Package/app: cold-store-reaper (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

items.body:
## Finding

cold-store-reaper caches a live Google OAuth **access token** in `state.json`, while the README describes `state.json` as "(no secrets)" and the file is written without the restrictive permissions the package applies to real credentials. Anyone or anything that can read `state.json` (backups, sync tools, another process in a less-protected home) holds a working Drive bearer token for its lifetime (~1h).

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #923 (cold-store-reaper v1), 2026-10-25; verified on current main (`92d0c6ee`).

## Evidence

- `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/README.md:52`: `state.json # folder IDs + cached access token (no secrets)` — the sentence contradicts itself: a cached access token is a credential.
- `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py:332` (in `access_token()`): `state["access_token"] = token`, persisted via `save_state()` (lines 228-229) → `_write_json()` (line 207), a plain `path.write_text(...)` with no mode restriction.
- Contrast the package's own credential handling: `_write_private_json()` writes `credentials.json` (client secret + refresh token) with `os.open(..., 0o600)` and an explicit chmod. The access token gets neither treatment.
- The only hardening is `init()` chmodding the home directory to `0o700` (line ~191 area) — that does not run on later invocations, and `$COLD_STORE_HOME` may point at a directory the tool did not create.
- Note the v2 D1 code in the same file is careful to take `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` "from the environment only; it is never stored" — the Drive access token deserves the same rule.

## Why it matters

A short-lived token is still a live credential: with `drive.file` scope it can read/modify everything the cold-store app owns — which is the entire archive. The "(no secrets)" label invites copying `state.json` into places secrets must never go (a synced folder, a debug bundle, a repo).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The access token is no longer persisted in `state.json` (keep it in memory only), OR `state.json` is written with `0o600` permissions via the existing private-write helper and the README stops claiming "(no secrets)".
- [ ] README's file-layout table accurately describes what `state.json` contains.
- [ ] Existing tests still pass; a test or check confirms no token value lands in `state.json` under the chosen design (if in-memory-only).

— filed by the pr-diff-review job (PR #923); triage via the repo-health queue pilot.

items.title: home(openclaw): gateway restart-race durability + heartbeat check fixes
items.body: ## Why The OpenClaw gateway died 2026-11-04 21:15 and stayed down ~24h. Root cause, from the gateway log + unit state: a system switch restarted the gateway while the OpenCode server had not yet rewritten `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json`; the unit's `ExecStartPre` (facade-auth-materialize) failed instantly, five times inside the default 10s start-limit window, and systemd parked the unit as `start-limit-hit`. The service record reappeared 3 minutes later; nothing ever retried the gateway. Separately, `HEARTBEAT.md` check 1 still curled the retired per-CLI proxies (18748/18746) as "the model's own lifelines". 18746 is dead since the facade rewire (opencode#1153), so every heartbeat since has had a failing first check — the Nov 4 "fleet proxy down" alerts were this stale check firing, and it would keep firing. ## Changes - **ExecStartPre waits**: up to ~3 min for the service record to yield a password before failing loudly. - **Unit durability**: `StartLimitIntervalSec=600`, `StartLimitBurst=30`, `RestartSec=5s`; ordered `After=opencode.service` (no Wants — the server has its own enablement). - **Heartbeat**: `skipWhenBusy=true` (upstream heartbeat docs recommend it on constrained hosts; stops heartbeats colliding with fleet work / dying on requests-in-flight). - **HEARTBEAT.md**: check 1 now verifies the facade model list (`127.0.0.1:13420/v1/models` with the materialized auth file); check 2 includes the `opencode` service. - **CHANNELS.md**: updated to reality — Slack live since 2026-10-26 (was described as pending Drew's setup); Telegram is not in the plugin load list at all. ## Verification Activation + gateway restart + heartbeat proof runs land with this change; results are reported on the OpenClaw fix thread. Rollback = revert; the previous rendered config backup is kept on the laptop. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Improvements** * The gateway now waits for OpenCode credentials before starting and retries with more resilient timing. * Health checks now verify that OpenCode is active and responding with route information. * Model routing now uses the OpenCode server instead of the retired proxy. * **Documentation** * Updated channel guidance with Slack, Control UI/WebChat, CLI, and ACP status and setup details. * Added SearXNG search and research plugin information, including its availability without API keys.

items.body:
# pm-stack(grist): no supported API path to extend a Choice column's options

Filed from direct experience, 2026-10-26 (Drew: "make an issue documenting what you wished it would do").

## What happened
Adding the `id` area to the Program roadmap required extending the Area column's Choice list in the Grist doc. The REST API refused: `/apply` with `UpdateColumn` returns "'UpdateColumn' actions are not controlled" — the doc's access rules reject schema changes even for the SOPS-managed admin API key that can freely read/write all data. The only working route was: stop the Grist container, edit the doc's SQLite directly (`_grist_Tables_column.widgetOptions`), restart, verify. It worked and a backup was taken first, but no routine change should need database surgery.

## What I wished it did
- A supported, authenticated way for a doc owner/admin to modify column options (at minimum Choice lists) via the API — either by making access rules able to *grant* schema actions to a role instead of rejecting them as uncontrolled, or a dedicated admin endpoint/CLI for column metadata.
- Access rules that distinguish data edits from schema edits, so "this key may manage schema" is an expressible policy.

## To investigate first
Whether the block is our doc's access-rules configuration (fixable in config) or a Grist OSS limitation (then this becomes an upstream feature request + a documented local workaround: the stop/edit/restart runbook, kept with the pm-stack docs). Either way the end state is: scripted choice-list edits with no direct SQLite writes.

Context: doc `czYHYKgG9SHcm9CPwiKEq1` (Program roadmap), Grist OSS v1.7.21 pinned in `pm-stack/grist/compose.yml`.

## Acceptance criteria

- One of the issue's two end states is reached and recorded here: either (a) an upstream Grist path (newer version or API action) supports extending a Choice column's options via the REST API and is adopted/pinned, or (b) a documented local workaround exists — the stop/edit/restart runbook kept with the pm-stack docs — so choice-list edits are scripted end to end.
- Either way: no direct SQLite writes to the Grist document database are part of the procedure.
- The runbook/adoption note names the Grist version it was verified against (currently OSS v1.7.21).

items.title: impl(pm-stack): browser-dependent quota watchdog core — disk state, failure classes, repair ladder

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

items.body:
Implements the watchdog core from the design in #6031 (browser-dependent quota watchdog). Scope is the **generic** machinery only — no provider specifics; Mistral is adapter #1 on top of this (openchamber issue, linked from #6031).

## What to build

In `pm-stack` (this repo), deployed on the laptop beside the gatherer:

1. **Watchdog oneshot + timer** (`pm-stack/systemd/`): runs on the gatherer's 15-minute rhythm, offset (e.g. `*:3/15`) so it judges fresh producer documents. Oneshot discipline like the existing laptop watchdog family (laptop-backups-watchdog code#1841, codex-remote-control-watchdog code#1845).
2. **State file** `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-watchdog-state.json` — atomic tmp+rename writes; per-source health record: `lastAttemptAt`, `lastSuccessAt`, `consecutiveFailures`, `currentClass`, sanitized `lastDetail`, `cooldownUntil`, `repairLog` (last 20), `incident` refs. **Nothing decision-relevant lives in process memory** — this is code#5928's lesson applied from day one (cross-tick cooldown + failure counts on disk).
3. **Failure-class evaluation:** read each registered source's `~/atlas/<provider>-export/latest.json` + the gatherer heartbeat; classify into `session-expired` / `cookie-missing` / `endpoint-changed` / `browser-down` / `cdp-unreachable` / `rate-limited` / `unknown` (producer pre-classifies its own failures; the watchdog owns classes the producer cannot see, e.g. missing document, browser process state).
4. **Repair ladder executor** with per-rung attempt caps (max 2 per incident) and a persisted repair log, cheapest first: (0) rate-limit cooldown honored from disk; (1) retry next tick (no-op rung); (2) CDP session re-validation against the live laptop browser (cookie **presence by name**; in-page fetch re-run — the cookie value is not read into the process; extraction only for adapters that declare a header-token path, value → fleet secrets by registered name only); (3) browser re-login driver via the provider's own SSO flow using the browser's standing Google session — stops dead at a human-only challenge and marks the incident **human-blocked**. Rung 4 (escalation) is the sibling escalation issue, invoked from here.
5. **Adapter loader:** read per-provider adapter files (`pm-stack/exporters/adapters/`) — origins allowlist, CDP port, data-path order, cookie names, login hints, class map, thresholds. The core contains zero provider names.
6. **Producer scaffolding:** a forkable producer template from the retired Meta producer (`~/atlas/meta-quota-export/meta-quota-export.mjs` on the laptop — CDP plumbing, tab ownership per code#5121, per-call timeouts, failure-class exit codes, atomic latest.json + history.jsonl), landing producer source in `pm-stack/exporters/`; plus the gatherer `FILE_EXPORTS` registration step documented/wired for each adopted source.
7. **Health history:** append per-tick per-source observations to `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-watchdog-history.jsonl` (interim); emit into the usage snapshot pipeline once code#4889's laptop path bug is fixed (do not block on it).

## Safety bounds (from the design)

Never writes quota data; never changes credentials other than re-storing an extracted session under its registered secret name; browser automation only against adapter allowlist origins, read endpoints + login flow only; no secret value in any log, state field, or document; login attempt caps double as account-lockout protection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Watchdog oneshot + timer installed on the laptop and ticking on the gatherer cadence; state file written atomically each tick and surviving across invocations (demonstrated over ≥3 consecutive ticks).
- [ ] A synthetic broken source (fixture adapter + producer stub) walks the ladder: retry → CDP re-validation → re-login attempt → escalation hand-off, with each rung's attempt recorded in `repairLog` and caps honored (no rung attempted >2× per incident).
- [ ] A `rate-limited` fixture sets `cooldownUntil` on disk and the next tick honors it without any browser action (the #5928 regression test, in effect).
- [ ] Human-only challenge fixture marks the incident human-blocked and the state carries the surfacing flag the orchestration/stewardship sweeps read.
- [ ] Quiet when healthy: a healthy source produces no output beyond journal/state/history records.
- [ ] Tests name their oracles per the testing doctrine (state-machine invariants for the ladder are a natural PBT/MBT fit).

Related: #6031 (design), #1260 (self-healing umbrella), #5928 (cross-tick state), #4889 (snapshot history path).

items.title: atlas search worker: Cloudflare Worker + per-query Durable Object embedding/result cache over the shard fan-out (successor surface for #5755)
items.body:
## What Drew ordered (2026-11-06 22:48 CST, verbatim substance)

Build the cross-database search surface as a **Cloudflare Worker** that pulls **all databases** for search; for each search query it **stores a Durable Object**, **automatically inserts the query as an embedding**, and **caches the result — for now, indefinitely** (no TTL/expiry).

This is the successor surface for the Atlas shard consumer wiring in #5755 (slice 1 merged in #6661; rehomed as `fleet serve search` in #6674). It supersedes the 2026-11-05 "Ask-the-ledger" direction (Cloudflare AI Search / AutoRAG over R2 snapshots + a query/miss ledger DB): Drew replaced the managed-AI-Search design with this explicit Worker + Durable Object + embedding cache design. The AI Search proposal is **not** being built; this issue is the record of what replaced it.

## Architecture (v1)

**Components**

1. **Cloudflare Worker** (`pkgs/atlas-search/worker/`) — the only public edge. Inbound gate: a shared bearer secret checked in the Worker (constant-time compare); not public-open. (Cloudflare Access in front of the Worker hostname is a follow-up hardening note below.)
2. **Durable Object class `QueryCache`** — one DO per distinct query. DO name = `sha256(normalized_query || config_fingerprint)` where the fingerprint pins `{ceiling: "personal", model_rev, vec_table, trunc: 0, k}` so a cache entry can never be served across different effective ceilings or embedding spaces (the same rule the search service applies to job dedupe).
3. **The fleet search service** (`fleet serve search` / `atlas-search serve`, laptop loopback :18760) remains the fan-out engine: it discovers the shard set from the Turso Platform API (only `atlas-core-*` databases), reads each candidate's `atlas_manifest` self-description (tier, topic, part, expected chunks), enforces per-client tier ceilings, embeds the query with the one shared resident embedder, runs the parallel cosine scan + merge/rerank. **The Worker keeps no shard list of its own** — new databases join the fan-out by existing in the Turso org with the `atlas-core-` prefix and a manifest; the Worker inherits the set through the service.
4. **Reachability**: the service is exposed to the Worker through the existing `amd-6-pm-stack` Cloudflare Tunnel as `atlas-search.security.cab` → `localhost:18760`, fronted by a Cloudflare Access application whose only policy is a **service token** the Worker presents (`CF-Access-Client-Id`/`CF-Access-Client-Secret`). The tunnel hostname without the service token is rejected by Access before it reaches the laptop.

**Miss path** (first time a query is seen)

1. Worker normalizes the query, computes the DO key, asks the DO for its entry → miss.
2. Worker calls the service's new **`POST /v1/embed`** (added by this work to both `server.rs` copies, parity-guarded): the service's shared embedder returns the production query vector. The Worker stores `{query, normalized_query, embedding, model, model_rev, dims, created_at}` in the DO **first** — the DO is born holding the query's embedding, per Drew's spec, even if the search below then fails.
3. Worker calls `POST /v1/search` (sync one-shot) with the dedicated **`cf-worker` service client** (see boundary below) → merged, reranked results.
4. Worker stores `{result, searched_at, fanout_ms, embed_ms}` in the DO and returns the result with `cache: "miss"` and the timings.

**Hit path**

- The DO returns the stored result verbatim; the fleet service is never contacted. Response carries `cache: "hit"`, the original `searched_at`, and a `hit_count` the DO increments. This is the proof surface: a hit must be byte-identical to the miss response's result and must not move any counter on the service side.

**Retention**

- **Indefinite.** No TTL, no eviction in v1 — Drew's "for now". DO storage is the ledger of every query ever asked through this surface. A future eviction policy (size/LRU) is a deliberate follow-up (filed separately), not a v1 behavior.

## Embedding source — decision and why

**The fleet embedder** (the service's resident ONNX session): model `Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0` pinned at rev `95c2741480856aa9666782eb4afe11959938017f`, query prompt `"query: "`, production vector table `vec_snowflake_m_v2_768_f32` — **768 dimensions**, full width (trunc = 0).

**Workers AI is rejected**: its 384-dim `@cf/baai/bge-small-en-v1.5` lives in a different embedding space (and a different width). Cosine similarity across embedding spaces is meaningless; a Worker-side embedding that cannot be compared against the corpus vectors would silently corrupt every ranking. Any edge embedding must reproduce the corpus's exact space, and the only artifact that does that today is the pinned Snowflake session in the fleet service.

Correction to older notes: several records describe the corpus as "384-dim Snowflake". Production is **768-dim** (`vec_snowflake_m_v2_768_f32` in the live service config; 384 was a Matryoshka truncation option from the Python era, never the production width).

## Secret-tier boundary

- The Worker authenticates to the search service as a dedicated client, **`cf-worker`, with `ceiling_cap: "personal"`** — the service mechanically caps it to the Public + Internal tiers. The Secret tier is unreachable through this client no matter what the Worker asks for.
- The Worker holds **no Turso credentials** and never receives secret-tier shard data, so nothing secret can enter a Durable Object — neither chunk content nor embeddings of secret chunks.
- The `drew-cli` client (`secret-bearing` cap) stays laptop-local and is not used by anything in this build. Secret-tier search remains a laptop-side-only operation, exactly as today.

## What v1 deliberately leaves out

- **Filters / FTS interplay** — the fan-out runs the service's default hybrid search; classification/date filters and the FTS answer remain #6665.
- **Hydration (`--expand`)** — results are the service's standard envelope; expansion remains #6664.
- **Serve-mode snapshot-id integration** — remains #6666.
- **Eviction policy** for the indefinite cache — follow-up issue (Drew: "for now").
- **Access in front of the Worker hostname itself** — v1 gate is the in-Worker bearer check; recorded as a hardening follow-up.
- The live proof in this issue advances #6662 only for the `personal` ceiling path through the Worker; #6662 stays open for its remaining parity scope.

## Open questions (recorded, proceeded on defaults)

- Worker hostname: default `atlas-search` on the account's `workers.dev` subdomain; a custom domain can be bound later without changing the design.
- Whether the DO should also store the FTS match expression / branch pools for debugging: default no — result + embedding + provenance only.

## Proof required (acceptance)

- Deployed Worker + DO; a real query run twice: first response `cache: "miss"` with fan-out executed (service-side evidence), DO created holding a 768-dim embedding; second response `cache: "hit"`, byte-identical result, served from the DO with no service contact; timings for both; DO state read back through the Worker's gated inspect endpoint.

items.body:
Follow-up C from the Durable Object jurisdiction investigation on #2061
(doc: `doc/2026-10-29T11-43-02Z_investigation_do_jurisdiction_pinning/`, §5 and §1.5).

Parent epic: #2056. Context: #2044.

Needs a Cloudflare account to deploy a scratch Worker — not doable from a repo-only worker session. Two halves: code mechanics (small PoC) and a written vendor ask (not code).

## Half 1 — PoC (one deployed scratch Worker, no user data)

1. `idFromName(name)` vs `jurisdiction("eu").idFromName(name)` produce different IDs in this account (docs assert it; confirm).
2. `ctx.id.jurisdiction` reads back `eu` inside the object, including from an alarm; confirm both `undefined` cases (unrestricted namespace; alarm scheduled before 2026-03-15).
3. A mismatched namespace/ID pair throws; an unrestricted namespace silently accepts a foreign ID (the failure mode the design guards against).
4. Export from an `eu` object, import into a `us` object: signatures still verify (migration path).
5. R2: create an `eu`-jurisdiction bucket, confirm the Worker binding needs the `jurisdiction` field and that the S3 jurisdiction endpoint cannot reach outside the jurisdiction.

## Half 2 — the written ask to Cloudflare (blocks any DPA that claims EU residency)

The docs guarantee the *object* "only run[s] and store[s] data within a region" and that it is never migrated out of the jurisdiction's data-centre list. They do **not** say that DO SQLite's storage replication path stays inside the jurisdiction:

- SQLite commits are forwarded to **five follower machines, each in a different physical data center**, and WAL batches/snapshots go to **object storage** ([blog](https://blog.cloudflare.com/sqlite-in-durable-objects/)). No jurisdiction statement appears in that post.
- Point-in-time recovery / bookmark retention: jurisdiction-confined? Not documented either way.
- Does `fedramp` jurisdiction for Durable Objects require a separate entitlement (R2's FedRAMP jurisdiction explicitly does; DO's docs say nothing)?

Ask Cloudflare support/account team in writing and record the answer on this issue. A negative or evasive answer changes the hosted edition's residency claim, so this is not optional polish.

## Acceptance

- PoC results recorded as a comment (or short doc) with what was observed, including failures.
- The vendor answer, or the exact question as sent plus the date, recorded here.
- Any gap the answer exposes filed as an issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PoC results recorded here (or in a short doc): all five Half-1 mechanics confirmed or the failure recorded, including both ctx.id.jurisdiction undefined cases
- [ ] The Cloudflare written ask (Half 2) sent verbatim and dated on this issue; the vendor answer recorded when it arrives
- [ ] Any residency gap the answer exposes is filed as its own issue

items.body:
## Phase 2 — Cloudflare edge relay: push that survives the stack

Design: `pm-stack-notifications-design-2026-11-11.md` (goal keep-the-four-repos-healthy, files/). Depends on Phase 1: #8568. Context: #1254 / #3676 (the laptop-side throat + Web Push this mirrors).

### The decision (go / no-go on the Cloudflare move)

- **NO-GO: moving the board / aggregator itself to Workers.** Every primary data source is laptop-local and tailnet-only (OpenCode :13420, queue broker :4801, Kaneo Postgres, projector DB, `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/*`). An edge board would be a cache of a dead source at exactly the moment it matters, and the board's job is live local state.
- **GO: a small edge notification relay** — one Worker + one Durable Object (`pm-notify`). The notification path is the one piece that must survive the laptop being down, and it is tiny: events in, subscriptions, push sends, answers in. The fleet already operates Workers (webhook-gateway on workers.dev, infra/github-backup/worker, pkgs/github-ci/worker, pkgs/id/hosted-worker), wrangler is packaged in-repo, and a day-to-day CF API token already lives in Bitwarden by name.

### Shape

- The aggregator throat mirrors every push-worthy event (incident raised/escalated, needs-drew raised, quota wall) to the Worker via authenticated POST (shared secret, same pattern as the throat intake token). The DO stores the mirror log + a subscription mirror.
- The laptop stack sends a heartbeat POST every ~60s. The DO sets an alarm on each heartbeat; a missed heartbeat window (~2 missed beats) fires `stack.silent`: the DO itself sends a Web Push ("the PM stack is down", with since-when) using the mirrored subscriptions and a VAPID keypair whose private key lives as a Worker secret. This is the dead-man's switch — no cron, no laptop, no Muse in the path.
- Edge answer intake: notification action taps and answer pages are served by the Worker from DO state (question + full option list), so Drew can answer while the laptop is down. Answers are stored in the DO and flushed to the aggregator's answers outbox (Phase 1 path) on the next heartbeat/event contact; if the laptop is up, the Worker can also forward immediately through the existing tunnel ingress pattern.
- Dual-send discipline during transition: for classes the edge owns (`stack.silent` only, at first) the laptop never sends; for mirrored classes the laptop remains the sender and the edge is a silent mirror until a later, separately-reviewed cutover.

### Acceptance (Drew's terms)

- Stop the whole laptop stack (or kill the tunnel) → a "stack down" push reaches Drew's phone in under 2 minutes with zero cron and zero Muse involvement.
- Answer a needs-drew question from the push while the laptop is down → when the stack returns, the ledger shows it answered and the blocked task unblocks; nothing is lost or double-applied.
- Stack recovers → one "recovered" push naming the downtime length; no duplicate down pushes for the same episode.
- The page-health-push cron narrows the day this ships: its page checks retire (the DO owns them) and it becomes a daily canary only — is the DO itself alive and did it receive yesterday's heartbeats.

items.title: Design + PoC: event-driven Slack collector (Socket Mode) to replace archer-slack-review polling

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: kind/design

items.body:
archer-slack-review polls a watermark every 15 min (~100K input/run × ~96 runs/day ≈ 9.6M/day) and usually finds nothing. Replace the polling with an event-driven collector (Drew approved 2026-10-29):

- A small service using Slack Socket Mode (outbound WebSocket — no public endpoint needed; Cloudflare Worker + Events API is the off-box alternative) appends messages, replies, and reactions from the watched channels to a local store.
- The review job wakes ONLY when the store has new items (hook/signal), reads just the delta, and acts.
- Placement per the flake rule (developing-today/code flake if on the laptop; sandbox systemd if on the sandbox). The service is deterministic — no LLM in the collection path.

PoC scope: the #alignment channel end-to-end (collect → store → wake → review). Success: quiet-day agent cost ~0; no missed Aster replies over a 3-day parallel run against the existing poller. Afterwards, generalize the pattern to other watermark polls.

items.body:
Umbrella for what the 2026-11-05 OpenClaw fix pass (gateway death + heartbeat root-cause; PRs #6142/#6151/#6162) deliberately left queued, with the evidence for each.

## 1. Activation queue (blocked by #6156 — main's HM generation doesn't evaluate since #6146)

Merged and waiting for ONE gateway restart once #6156 is fixed:
- PR #6151: nix-openclaw pin 4b261b08 → 26516d99 (app pin still 2026.10.7 — upstream nix-openclaw has not published a 2026.10.10 pin; their Unreleased changelog already carries .10 pin validation, so the pin bump should follow within days; bump the day it appears) + memory-lancedb `autoCapture: true`.
- PR #6162: memory-lancedb `hooks.allowConversationAccess = true` (without it autoRecall/autoCapture hooks are blocked — the memory DB is at 0 entries).
Post-activation proofs owed: gateway health + Slack connected, `openclaw ltm stats` > 0 after a real conversation, a memory_recall hit from an agent turn, 3 wake-triggered heartbeat runs ok, version string from the new unit's store path.

## 2. memory-wiki plugin (evaluate + likely enable)

Disabled today. Upstream documents it as the companion to memory-lancedb (only one plugin owns the memory SLOT; wiki runs alongside) and the 2026.10.10 release notes show active Memory Wiki work. It turns Shed's accumulated memories into a browsable wiki in the workspace — the inspectable surface for the memory system we just switched on. Enable in home/openclaw (runtimePlugins + entry) in the same activation batch as §1 if evaluation stays favorable.

## 3. Vendored summarize plugin is not loading

`home/openclaw/default.nix` wires the vendored summarize plugin via `customPlugins` (fetchTree pin), and the gateway PATH contains the summarize 0.21.14 CLI — but `openclaw plugins list` on the live gateway shows **no summarize plugin** in either the enabled or disabled list. (#1030, the bundled-plugin re-enable, is closed/superseded by the vendored approach.) Diagnose why the custom plugin doesn't register; the summarize capability was a Drew request from 2026-10-26.

## 4. Channel completion menu (each needs the named Drew act; nothing else blocks)

Current state: Slack LIVE (socket, DM allowlist = Drew). Plugins for discord/whatsapp/matrix/signal/telegram are packaged; no credentials for them exist in the vault (checked 2026-11-05: only `openclaw.slack-*` present).
- **WhatsApp**: Drew scans a QR with his phone (`openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp` on the laptop).
- **Telegram**: Drew talks to @BotFather under his Telegram account to mint a bot token (file as `openclaw.telegram-bot-token`); the telegram plugin also needs adding to `runtimePlugins` in home/openclaw.
- **Signal**: Drew links signal-cli (QR/device link with his phone).
- **Discord**: a bot application + token under Drew's Discord account (developer portal), filed as `openclaw.discord-token`; then a channels.discord block like Slack's.
- **Matrix**: an account on a homeserver for Shed (registration is the step), filed by name; then channels.matrix config.
Per Drew's 2026-11-05 latitude ("setup whatever for claw"), each of these is a standing go once the named act exists. Email is explicitly OUT: no email sending about any of this, and email is not to be wired as a notification/delivery path (the imap plugin stays disabled).

## 5. Gateway-death alerting gap

The 2026-11-04 death was silent for ~24h: when the gateway is down, nothing off-box notices (the heartbeat dies with it). Candidate: a fleet-side watch (stewardship visibility or the morning readout) that checks the gateway health endpoint / unit state from outside the laptop and surfaces a dead gateway in the main chat. Any watch must NOT live inside OpenClaw itself.

## 6. heartbeat.skipWhenBusy

Upstream-recommended for constrained hosts; the nix-openclaw generated schema (both the old pin and 26516d99) has no such option. Re-check after the 2026.10.10 pin lands; add when expressible. The config carries a NOTE comment marking the spot.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Activation batch (§1) lands after #6156 is fixed and ONE gateway restart: post-activation proofs recorded here — gateway health + Slack connected, `openclaw ltm stats` > 0 after a real conversation, a memory_recall hit from an agent turn, 3 wake-triggered heartbeat runs ok, version string from the new unit's store path.
- [x] memory-wiki (§2): evaluation verdict recorded; if favorable, enabled in home/openclaw in the activation batch.
- [x] Vendored summarize plugin (§3): diagnosed — it registers in `openclaw plugins list` and the summarize capability works, or the gap is dispositioned with a named cause.
- [ ] Channel menu (§4): each channel is either live or waiting on exactly the named Drew act listed in the body; no email wiring (explicitly out).
- [ ] Gateway-death alerting (§5): an off-box watch (outside OpenClaw) surfaces a dead gateway in the main chat — proven by one drill or a real detection.
- [ ] heartbeat.skipWhenBusy (§6): re-checked after the 2026.10.10 pin lands; added when the schema expresses it, or the blocker re-recorded.

items.body:
## Session error wave 2026-11-07 21:00–22:00 CST — _claude credential blanked; 49 sessions dead, still ongoing

**Diagnosis (session-minder triage, 2026-11-07 ~22:15 CST, from laptop opencode.db route_attempt + minder snaps):**

- 49 sessions newly errored across the 21:00 / 21:10–21:35 / 21:40 / 22:00 lane batches (failed in top-200: 2 → 51). Error class: **656 of 664 post-switch Claude-model attempts are `_claude` Authentication failures** — "Claude Code is not signed in on this machine: no OAuth credential in ~/.claude/.credentials.json and no CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in the environment." Since the current server started, `_claude` is **656 attempts / 0 successes**.
- **Root cause:** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` was rewritten at **19:02 CST** with EMPTY `accessToken` (len 0), EMPTY `refreshToken` (len 0), `expiresAt` 0 (subscription metadata retained: max, sign_in). Preceded by the 18:35 CST revoked-OAuth 401. Whatever wrote the file at 19:02 persisted empty tokens over a live credential.
- The old fastlane server held a working in-memory credential, so Claude legs kept working until the **nixos-rebuild switch restarted the server at 21:04:34 CST** (base unit opencode.service, 2.0.30+4b2fc8a). The new process read the blanked file → total _claude outage from that moment. The switch exposed the blanking; it did not cause it. The speed/_muse config edit (22:04) is exonerated: later, different provider, no restart.
- **Amplification:** sonnet-plan made 263 decisions since the switch, ALL choosing `_claude/claude-sonnet-5-5` — the `_antigravity` Claude leg is quota-closed (AG Claude+GPT weekly 100%) and never attempted, so sonnet-plan has exactly one live candidate and no failover target when it auth-fails. Sessions on Luna/Vibe/DeepSeek legs survived (146 succeeded). This is the #7073 failure shape at fleet scale.
- **Still ongoing** at 22:11 CST: 72 _claude auth failures in the trailing 10 minutes. Every new batch will keep dying on Claude legs until the credential is restored.

## Fix
1. **Re-provision the Claude Code OAuth credential fleet-side on the laptop** (2026-11-06 restore route; the refresh token is also empty, so a refresh alone cannot recover it — a sign-in/OAuth flow is required). Cf. #6120 (Claude auth auto-renewal gap).
2. **Restart opencode.service** so the provider re-reads the credential; then restart the OpenClaw gateway (known coupling) and verify both; spot-check `_claude` attempts succeeding in route_attempt.
3. **Fork defect (developing-today-forks/opencode):** a credential write must never persist empty tokens over an existing credential — on refresh failure, preserve the existing file. Whatever wrote empties at 19:02 CST is the bug.
4. Failover amplification is tracked on #7073 — this issue is its largest exhibit; no duplicate work there.

Acceptance: `_claude` success attempts > 0 in route_attempt after restore; a lane batch completes with failed-count back to baseline; the minder's next check shows no new provider.auth session deaths.


## Acceptance criteria
- The problem described above is confirmed against current main (reproduced or traced to the named code path), or the issue is closed with that evidence.
- A fix/implementation addressing the described behaviour is merged via PR referencing this issue, with tests naming their oracle where the change has meaningful invariants.
- Related/sibling issues from the same filing batch are cross-linked and any dependency is recorded as a native blocked-by relation.

items.body:
# proxy-supervise: unrecognized arguments are silently ignored — a typo'd `--dry-rnu` starts/rolls real proxies, and a typo'd `--statuz` reconciles instead of reporting status

## Summary

`bin/proxy-supervise.mjs` (the supervisor that starts/stops/rolls the local proxy instances on its timer) parses its CLI flags by membership only and never rejects an argument it does not recognize:

- `bin/proxy-supervise.mjs:603-629` — `const args = process.argv.slice(2)`; flags are read with `args.indexOf('--config')` / `args.indexOf('--only')` (:604-608), `args.includes('--status')` (:620) and `args.includes('--dry-run')` (:629). There is no allowlist check over `args` anywhere in `main()`; the only validation is that `--config` is present.

So `proxy-supervise.mjs --config <cfg> --dry-rnu` is silently treated as a real reconcile: it acquires the per-proxy lock and **starts a new proxy instance** (or rolls/stops the existing one). Worse, the read-only path has the same flaw in reverse: `--statuz` (a typo of `--status`) falls through to a full reconcile instead of printing status. Both exit 0.

This is the same defect class already filed for the sibling deploy/install scripts — #3264 (pkarr-worker `deploy.mjs`), #3278 (opencode-claimant `install.mjs`), #3281 (id-mail worker `deploy.mjs`), #3287 (github-backup worker `deploy.mjs`) — but this script is a different, long-lived operator tool none of them covers. The repo's shell tools already meet the stricter standard: `lib/bws-to-sops.sh` dies on `unknown argument` and `scripts/stage-docs.sh` exits 1 on an unknown option.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-supervise/` (proxy-supervise.mjs copied verbatim; sha256 `1926654cf1148a65a59e6b0c05f66a42552307de68d194153fcefbe25e7252bb`, matching main `b56ccda5`), with a fixture config in a temp dir (one proxy whose command is a tiny HTTP server answering `/health`, `stateDir`/`endpointDir` inside the probe dir, port 18999):

- Control — `--dry-run`: exit 0, action `would-start`, port stays FREE, no state or endpoint files written.
- `--dry-rnu`: exit 0, action **`started`** — a real server process (pid recorded in `state/probeproxy.json`), port 18999 HEALTHY afterwards.
- `--bogus-flag`: exit 0, identical real start (new pid, state file written, port healthy).
- `--statuz`: exit 0, action `started` — the intended read-only status check reconciled and started the proxy instead.

(The probe cleaned up every instance it started; final port check FREE.)

## Why it matters

This supervisor owns the lifecycle of the local proxy fleet: a real reconcile can start, roll, drain and stop live proxy processes. A one-character typo in either safety flag — the preview flag `--dry-run` or the read-only `--status` — silently becomes the mutating operation, with a success exit code and a normal JSON result line, so the operator has no signal anything beyond a preview/status just happened.

## Acceptance criteria

- Any argument that is not `--config <path>`, `--only <name>`, `--status` or `--dry-run` makes the script exit non-zero with a usage error naming the offending argument, before any lock is taken or any reconcile runs.
- `--config` / `--only` with a missing value or a value that is another flag are rejected the same way.
- `--status`, `--dry-run`, and bare reconcile behavior is unchanged.
- A test (the script already has importable exports / a test file pattern in `bin/`) pins: unknown flag → non-zero exit + zero spawned processes; `--dry-run` → `would-start` only; `--statuz`-style typos do not fall through to reconcile.
