items.body:
Implementation piece 2 of #1511 (repo-universe issue tracker) — the scheduled checker. Depends on the inventory artifact (piece 1).

## Scope
- A scheduled, read-only checker (fleet cron, same home as the other read-only fleet checks) that, for every universe repo with `watch: issues`:
  - fetches issues via `gh api --paginate repos/<owner>/<name>/issues?state=all&since=<last-run watermark>` (issues endpoint; filter out pull requests),
  - diffs against a persisted state file (per repo: issue number → state, title, updated_at, html_url),
  - emits a delta report (new / changed / closed per repo) to the repo-health goal workspace and appends state.
- Watermark/state handling: first run baselines without reporting the full history as "new" (report counts only); a failed repo fetch is reported as an error line, never silently treated as zero issues.
- The checker performs NO writes to GitHub. Creating/updating tracking entries is piece 3's job; the delta report is its input.

## Acceptance
- Two consecutive runs with no upstream changes produce an empty delta and zero state churn beyond the run timestamp.
- A test issue opened in dezren39/hatch-personal appears in the next run's delta as `new`; closing it appears as `closed` on the following run.
- Runs unattended on its schedule and leaves a dated delta report per run.

Parent: #1511 (design posted there by queue task 1549).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A scheduled, read-only checker runs unattended for every universe repo with `watch: issues` and performs no writes to GitHub.
- [ ] Two consecutive runs with no upstream changes produce an empty delta and zero state churn beyond the run timestamp (the body's Acceptance bullets, restated here as the criteria section).
- [ ] A test issue opened in dezren39/hatch-personal appears in the next run's delta as `new`; closing it appears as `closed` on the following run.
- [ ] A failed repo fetch is reported as an error line in the delta report, never silently treated as zero issues.
- [ ] Each run leaves a dated delta report in the repo-health goal workspace and advances the persisted watermark/state.

items.body:
# id: next horizons — investigation + discussion with Drew (planning, not a work order)

Drew (2026-10-26): "We need to start preparing for further phases and next steps. Ensure there are designs either built or on the roadmap to be made... Investigate and find things we could do, and then another issue to discuss with me, and we'll come up with a plan." **This is that discussion issue. Nothing here starts until we agree a plan in the comments.**

## Where the design coverage stands today (checked 2026-10-26)
- Phases 0–11: designed and built; validation audits queued (#1075–#1078) to prove it.
- Phase 12: epic #534 runs each F-item through the research/design workflow before implementation; item issues exist for all of F12.1–F12.18. The two that most need design depth first: **F12.4 provider registry** (#1061 — the registry shape constrains everything) and **F12.10 scheduling/quotas** (#1067 — policy, not just code).
- Phase 13: client shells + capability providers; F13.1/F13.2 done, F13.3–F13.8 filed (#785–#790). No design docs yet for F13.6 native shells (#788) beyond the shell contract.
- Beyond Phase 13: **nothing is designed or roadmapped.** That's the gap this issue is for.

## Candidate directions worth a Phase 14+ (from the current architecture and open threads)
1. **Hosted worlds / always-on hosting** — worlds that live on a host (e.g. the basement cluster) instead of a participant's machine: persistence, backups/snapshot export, world DR, uptime. Builds on F12.11 multi-node and F12.13 replication.
2. **Discovery & federation** — the world directory (#812 feed is the seed), signed catalogs, cross-node invites, popularity/quality signals. Global chat exists; worlds are still islands.
3. **Program ecosystem** — share/fork Roc programs and template worlds, a gallery, one-click install into a world; provenance from F12.17 makes this safe to open up.
4. **More shells** — mobile/PWA shell with offline mode, native apps (#1072), the ratatui TUI (#1071), and hardware shells — the ESP32 wing line of work already running in the fleet could become a physical id terminal/input device.
5. **Agents in worlds** — agent participants as first-class programs: MCP bridge so an agent can join a world, read screens, act — id as a place agents and people share, not just people.
6. **Scale & performance hardening** — large-world stress program (entity counts, journal growth, bandwidth budgets), snapshot/compaction policy, chaos tests across nodes.
7. **Creator tooling & insight** — world analytics for authors, in-world search across worlds, moderation tooling for public worlds (needed before any public directory).

## Also on the table
- The dashboard build-out (#1239) — how much of the platform's operational picture belongs there vs in `id world doctor`-style CLI surfaces.

## Questions for Drew
- Which 1–2 themes feel like the real Phase 14? (My instinct: hosted worlds + discovery, because they turn id from a tool into a place — but agents-in-worlds is the most differentiating.)
- Local-first forever, or is a hosted tier an explicit goal?
- How public should discovery be at first — tailnet friends, invite-only catalogs, or open?
- Anything on your mind that isn't in the candidate list?

When we've talked it through here, the output is: chosen themes → design issues filed → roadmap "Later" section updated. Until then this stays `priority/low` discussion.

## Acceptance criteria

- A discussion with Drew in this issue's comments produces an agreed plan: which post-Phase-13 directions (from the candidate list or new ones) become Phase 14+ design work, and in what order.
